issues.title: Add Wi-Fi settings and cheat search, improve stability and fix Android CI
issues.body:
This adds Wi-Fi connection settings, searchable cheat selectors and reliability improvements for saves, audio and controls. It also fixes the GitHub Actions setup failure that prevented the previous submission from reaching compilation.

### User-facing changes

- **Wi-Fi connections:** configure three WFC slots and primary/secondary DNS addresses in Settings, and enable or disable slots from the pause menu. DSi edits persist both basic and extended connection blocks.
- **Setup and preferences:** guided BIOS/firmware setup, settings/layout backup and restore, and optional forward-only clock synchronization.
- **Controls and cheats:** hold-to-fast-forward, combination hotkeys, optional fast-forward muting and grouped cheat selectors. Interrupted touches and lost controller focus release held inputs.
- **Cheat search:** search folders, individual cheats and generated selector options. Matching text is highlighted; selecting a result opens the matching row or selector without enabling it. Results use lazy scrolling, and the query survives navigation and loading/restoration transitions.
- **Reliability:** improve save-write failure handling, audio restoration after resume, ROM icon loading and bounded 7z decoding memory. Also fixes LCD/scanline alignment, XML cheat import and temporary JNI references while listing DSiWare titles.

### Actions correction

- Explicitly request `platform-tools` instead of the unavailable SDK package `tools`.
- Update checkout, Java setup, Android setup and artifact upload to supported Node 24 versions across the Android workflows.
- Run unit tests and an ARM64 debug APK build for forks and pull requests with read-only repository permissions and no release-signing secrets.
- Restrict signed Nightly publication to upstream `master`; upload verification APKs from their actual build output path.
- Remove the nonexistent `setup-ndk` output reference and place the manual Play Store actor restriction on the job, where GitHub evaluates it.

### Credits and issue coverage

The search UI is adapted from [#1677](https://github.com/rafaelvcaetano/melonDS-android/pull/1677) by [takanuva15](https://github.com/takanuva15), whose coauthor credit is preserved. This extends that work to grouped/generated options and precise navigation. Also includes adaptations of #1606/#1608 (WailAbou), #1625 (dysprosium), #1648 (N3MI-DG), #1589 (DLCSharp), and selected side fixes from #1666 (corigne).

- Fixes #1678: temporary JNI references accumulating while listing DSiWare titles.
- Implements the settings/layout backup and restore requested in #264.
- Partially addresses audio resume (#1644/#1635), clock drift (#1652/#1604), and 7z scanning crashes (#1519/#1378). Optional fast-forward muting is a workaround for #1602; remaining device-specific symptoms and audible distortion are not claimed fixed.

### Core dependency

Companion core PR: https://github.com/rafaelvcaetano/melonDS-android-lib/pull/19. This proposal pins core commit `f950b5e69c1c72dd309ec7af6ad9261d0076e5fc`, whose source tree is unchanged from the previously tested core. Review the pair together; merge the core first and update the app's gitlink to the accepted revision if its SHA changes. WFC firmware editing does not require the optional hostname-override API.

### Validation and limits

- **Hosted Actions passed:** [Linux verification run](https://github.com/Umberto-DEV/melonDS-android/actions/runs/40112578134) completed **180 JVM tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped**, including the search regressions, and built the ARM64 debug APK against the pinned core. JUnit results and the APK were uploaded successfully. The SDK failure and deprecated-action warnings are gone.
- Additional checks: workflow YAML parsing, `git diff --check`, source-tree equality, dependency alignment and contributor attribution. Earlier native JNI/DNS test results remain applicable to the unchanged sources; those host tests were not rerun for this workflow update.
- The [separate upstream PR run](https://github.com/rafaelvcaetano/melonDS-android/actions/runs/40112753066) is awaiting a maintainer's approval to start. The fork run above validates this exact proposed commit.
- A prior Android build received five weeks of user testing on an AYN Thor. The additional fixes and search have automated coverage but have not received a new Thor acceptance test. No emulator or APK was installed during this resubmission.
- Android Lint is **not clean**: 278 errors in the recorded run versus 207 upstream, with the 71 additional errors all missing translations. The known JIT/interpreter framebuffer discrepancy also reproduces upstream. These limitations are not hidden or described as passing checks.

### Screenshots

Wi-Fi settings captured on an AYN Thor from the earlier tested build:

![Wi-Fi connection settings with primary and secondary DNS](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Umberto-DEV/melonDS-android/aedb719f56d50b5457c08de1172e166b23f5861e/docs/images/wfc-connection-settings.png)

![Wi-Fi connection settings overview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Umberto-DEV/melonDS-android/aedb719f56d50b5457c08de1172e166b23f5861e/docs/images/wfc-overview.png)

Supersedes #1681. The functional changes and community contributions are preserved; resubmission changes concern Actions, contribution metadata, screenshot filenames and the equivalent core revision.

issues.title: Map phone sleep/wake to DS lid close/open
issues.body:
## Summary

When the phone screen turns off, the DS lid close input is now triggered so the running game can play their sleep sound (if supported) before emulation is paused. 
On screen wake, the lid reopens allowing the game to play their wake sound.

On sleep, games have a 3s window to react on sleep before emulation is paused. There can be slight audio crunchiness during this window because of Android's handling : a service is used to keep the app in foreground which helps a lot.

It is not a necessary feature, but it's fun and makes the experience more immersive, especially on dual-screen handhelds like the Ayn Thor.

## Tested games 

Test devices : Ayn Thor, Samsung Galaxy S23+

Confirmed working with no issues : 

- New Super Mario Bros
- Scribblenauts
- Super Scribblenauts
- Super Mario 64 DS
- Castlevania: Portrait of Ruin
- Transformers: War for Cybertron
- The Legendary Starfy
- Yoshi's Island DS
- Mario vs Donkey Kong Mini-Land Mayhem
- Mario vs Donkey Kong 2 March of the Minis                                    

Full list of known games which play sounds on wake/sleep : https://niwanetwork.org/wiki/Sleep_Mode

issues.title: Fast-forward audio: fix crackling with dynamic rate matching, plus optional pitch preservation
issues.body:
# Fast-forward audio: fix crackling with dynamic rate matching, plus optional pitch preservation

## Problem

With fast-forward active, audio crackles badly and becomes unlistenable at higher speeds. Constant-speed playback is unaffected.

**Root cause.** The SPU produces samples at a rate tied to the emulated frame rate, while the audio hardware consumes them in real time through a fixed 48 kHz stream. The ring buffer between them is small (2048 stereo frames, ~43 ms). During fast-forward the SPU produces N× more samples per real second but the stream still consumes at 1×; the buffer overruns within a few callbacks, and the resulting overflow/underrun cycles are heard as crackling. The old code had no mechanism to reconcile the two rates: the resampling ratio was clamped to ±0.5 % regardless of speed, and the output was stretched or zero-filled whenever the buffer ran dry.

## Solution

Two layers: a rate-matching controller that fixes the crackling at every speed, and an opt-in pitch-preservation mode on top of it.

**Part 1 — dynamic rate-matching controller (always active).** The SPU output skew (the resampling ratio between the emulated clock and output samples) is adjusted so production tracks actual consumption. Pitch rises with the actual emulation speed — the traditional fast-forward sound — but the stream stays continuous and free of artifacts. Four cooperating parts:

1. **FPS feedforward** — the measured frame rate is converted to a target production ratio and smoothed with an EMA. On a fast-forward toggle or speed change, the controller seeds itself from the configured multiplier and applies the first fresh measurement directly, so the ratio is correct within one callback cycle.
2. **Fill-level feedback** — a small proportional correction (clamped to ±2 %, inaudible) holds the buffer near half full.
3. **High-water safety valve** — if the buffer still crosses 85 % capacity, one trim resets it to half, with rate-limited logging, a short feedback freeze, and a +2 % feedforward nudge so repeated trips self-correct the root estimate.
4. **Slew limiting** — the applied ratio moves at most ±1 % per callback, so pitch glides instead of stepping.

An additional setting mutes fast-forward audio above a chosen speed step (never, or above any of the fixed steps 1.5×–8×, matching the speed options), with hysteresis so it never chatters around the line; the default keeps audio audible.

**Part 2 — optional pitch preservation (opt-in, default off).** A second setting engages time-stretching so fast-forward keeps the original pitch at **every** fast-forward speed, via a vendored SoundTouch library (LGPL-2.1) under `app/src/main/cpp/soundtouch/`. The stretch path runs a tempo controller of the same four-part design as Part 1 (FPS feedforward, output-buffer feedback, slew limiting, safety valve), with tempo ≈ current emulation speed — pitch unchanged at any multiplier, including 8× and uncapped. To make room for high-speed production, the SPU ring buffer between the emulator and the stretcher is enlarged from 2048 to 8192 samples (lib submodule; production at 8× would otherwise overrun it within a few callbacks and drop samples). Save-state load, rewind, speed changes and stream rebuilds clear the stretcher and re-seed the controller. Known trade-offs, also stated in the setting summary: a brief silence while the stretcher refills on entry; on exit, a content jump of at most the current backlog.

**Constant-speed path is untouched** — the same fixed ratio as master, bit-for-bit. The shared state read by the audio callback (fast-forward flag, FPS, multiplier, threshold) is now atomic, ordered by the fast-forward flag.

## Testing

Real device (debug build):

- Fast-forward audio is continuous, no crackling; pitch preservation behaves as expected; constant-speed playback unaffected.
- Audio-to-video latency stays at a few tens of milliseconds and does not grow over time (the tempo feedback controls the stretcher's output buffer, whose unnoticed growth previously accumulated up to ~1 s during long fast-forward sessions).
- Performance on the same device, Pokémon HeartGold, software renderer + threaded video: fast-forward alone sustains 98 fps; with audio stretching enabled, 96 fps (~2 % lower).
- Includes one submodule change (SPU ring buffer size).

## Notes for reviewers

- The SPU APIs used (`GetOutputSize` / `TrimOutput` / `DrainOutput` / `SetOutputSkew`) already exist in the core; the only lib submodule change is the SPU output ring buffer size (one-line capacity formula), submitted as a companion pull request on melonDS-android-lib: https://github.com/rafaelvcaetano/melonDS-android-lib/pull/17 — the submodule pointer in this PR resolves once that one merges.
- Remaining tuning items (quickseek hard-coded off, backlog/valve thresholds) were validated on one device class; follow-up calibration may be needed from weaker-hardware reports.

issues.title: Restore sessions after Android process death
issues.body:
This is the follow-up I mentioned in #1624.

When Android kills melonDS while the device is sleeping, reopening the app now restores a private checkpoint instead of returning to the ROM list or restarting the BIOS. Automatic recovery is limited to the exact previous process and Android low-memory, resource, freezer, or SIGKILL exits. Prompted recovery disables Hardcore.

I reproduced the original path on an AYN Thor running Android 13 by forcing real LMKD pressure while the device was asleep. Android reported `LOW_MEMORY`; the ROM restored without a dialog, Hardcore remained enabled, animation and touch worked, and the next sleep checkpoint completed normally. Firmware recovery was also tested through the animated health screen and into the firmware menu.

The recovery policy and event framing have portable JVM tests run by a dedicated pull-request workflow.

issues.title: Sync RTC on lid open
issues.body:
This pull request introduces a new feature to synchronize the emulated Real Time Clock (RTC) with the device's system time when the lid is opened or when the app resumes. This feature is configurable via a new setting in the preferences, and the implementation spans both the native (C++) and Android (Kotlin) codebases. Additionally, it includes UI updates to expose the new option to users.

**RTC Synchronization Feature:**

* Added a new setting `syncRtcOnLidOpen` to `EmulatorConfiguration`, including support in the preferences, repository, and configuration builder (`EmulatorConfiguration.kt`, `SettingsRepository.kt`, `SharedPreferencesSettingsRepository.kt`, `MelonDSAndroidConfiguration.cpp`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-5bb865e4d4eee686a7486bfa894916e2c413bc69a2be8f1f3a75f7d8948edcfeR21) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-08ded61b6137f78805ffc40250a7ae01d2242660ed919f93c3413c594e862dddR33) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-363d6be5d2c60ac3982fe20ff675cedadb0d9b260b920b3464c54e3866c797b0R161) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-86c899d85598e47515d9ccc97d41e87eb13018eb46d7608b6b8af06a7e16ef7fR35) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-86c899d85598e47515d9ccc97d41e87eb13018eb46d7608b6b8af06a7e16ef7fR80) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-363d6be5d2c60ac3982fe20ff675cedadb0d9b260b920b3464c54e3866c797b0R184-R187) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-1e715e9b8a5a7c11958cfd17819b5f19bf9586e2b4235015e888be8e74147529R77)
* Implemented RTC synchronization logic in the native emulator: when the lid is opened (key release) and the setting is enabled, the emulator syncs its RTC with the system time (`MelonInstance.cpp`, `MelonInstance.h`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-06d687b708047a94ab42ad0d4a25bf7a1c0194eaf0ce5b4a3cef15b1e698b7d2R438-R440) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-06d687b708047a94ab42ad0d4a25bf7a1c0194eaf0ce5b4a3cef15b1e698b7d2R450-R454) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-594778dc8f73e9590d9ff1730845a94e5c065b3134b81273e673ee5540e9cb8fR45)
* Exposed a new JNI function and corresponding Kotlin binding to allow manual RTC sync from the Android layer (`MelonDSAndroidJNI.cpp`, `MelonEmulator.kt`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-9020d308eedc40b49ac45cfe398b264ccf6c25c04bfaf4cf486c1390b8f98b2eR502-R507) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4c8d27ea49e0c298f91609aa032ba2cbb80dfbf973090501dbd7288f9a8c6d00R94-R95)
* Added a method in `EmulatorManager` and its Android implementation to trigger RTC sync, and invoked this method automatically when the app resumes if the setting is enabled (`EmulatorManager.kt`, `AndroidEmulatorManager.kt`, `EmulatorActivity.kt`, `EmulatorViewModel.kt`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-60b9eb718d641aea74cdbc799bab8954defacf9d7a4513dcc4c9a3df9e0adcc9R36-R37) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2cea01aeebe24397ed96eb0f77a811092499ec0d7cd3baafc66070bd79887414R172-R175) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-6f0b4fe13614348166541ff2b99dad492547aa59f9194f22f9cd691120080144R710) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-ada03f22baee934a34034417ccaa292ed10ec87407d6ea18ffc53da921457802R378-R387)

**User Interface Updates:**

* Added a new switch preference to the system settings screen, with corresponding strings for the label and summary (`pref_system.xml`, `strings.xml`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-8255d9796a223248dbfa9f62a809aa6e6dc23436428d8d07625a0eae8a61b081R25-R31) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-5e01f7d37a66e4ca03deefc205d8e7008661cdd0284a05aaba1858e6b7bf9103R203-R204)

These changes allow users to keep the emulator's clock accurate by optionally syncing it with the device time on lid open or app resume, improving time-based emulation accuracy.

issues.title: Reduces fatal OutOfMemoryErrors on Ayn Thor and other recent devices when reading 7z files
issues.body:
The Ayn Thor can have 8GB (Lite/Base), 12GB (Pro) or 16GB (Max) of RAM, and has 8 CPU cores.

When running melonDS on my Thor, I was seeing immediate + constant crashes of the app when it first started up (as it started to display the list of games).  Usually only a few games are shown before melonDS crashes.

It appears that when there are more than a few compressed files in the ROM path (especially 7zip compressed), the app crashes with a `OutOfMemoryError` exception.

Example stack:

```
2025-11-04 11:58:31.501 12724-12751 AndroidRuntime          me.magnum.melonds.dev               E  FATAL EXCEPTION: DefaultDispatcher-worker-4 (Ask Gemini)
    Process: me.magnum.melonds.dev, PID: 12724
    java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Failed to allocate a 536870928 byte allocation with 25165824 free bytes and 504MB until OOM, target footprint 32592784, growth limit 536870912
        at org.tukaani.xz.ArrayCache.getByteArray(ArrayCache.java:155)
        at org.tukaani.xz.lz.LZDecoder.<init>(LZDecoder.java:25)
        at org.tukaani.xz.LZMA2InputStream.<init>(LZMA2InputStream.java:169)
        at org.tukaani.xz.LZMA2InputStream.<init>(LZMA2InputStream.java:135)
        at org.tukaani.xz.LZMA2InputStream.<init>(LZMA2InputStream.java:113)
        at org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.sevenz.LZMA2Decoder.decode(LZMA2Decoder.java:43)
        at org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.sevenz.Coders.addDecoder(Coders.java:228)
        at org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.sevenz.SevenZFile.buildDecoderStack(SevenZFile.java:747)
        at org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.sevenz.SevenZFile.reopenFolderInputStream(SevenZFile.java:1732)
        at org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.sevenz.SevenZFile.buildDecodingStream(SevenZFile.java:808)
        at org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.sevenz.SevenZFile.getInputStream(SevenZFile.java:1000)
        at me.magnum.melonds.common.romprocessors.SevenZRomFileProcessor.getNdsEntryStreamInFileStream(SevenZRomFileProcessor.kt:32)
        at me.magnum.melonds.common.romprocessors.CompressedRomFileProcessor.getRomFromUri(CompressedRomFileProcessor.kt:32)
        at me.magnum.melonds.impl.FileSystemRomsRepository.findCachedRomFiles(FileSystemRomsRepository.kt:235)
        at me.magnum.melonds.impl.FileSystemRomsRepository.access$findCachedRomFiles(FileSystemRomsRepository.kt:38)
        at me.magnum.melonds.impl.FileSystemRomsRepository$scanForNewRoms$1.invokeSuspend(FileSystemRomsRepository.kt:221)
        at me.magnum.melonds.impl.FileSystemRomsRepository$scanForNewRoms$1.invoke(Unknown Source:8)
        at me.magnum.melonds.impl.FileSystemRomsRepository$scanForNewRoms$1.invoke(Unknown Source:4)
        at kotlinx.coroutines.flow.SafeFlow.collectSafely(Builders.kt:61)
        at kotlinx.coroutines.flow.AbstractFlow.collect(Flow.kt:230)
        at me.magnum.melonds.impl.FileSystemRomsRepository.loadCachedRoms(FileSystemRomsRepository.kt:210)
        at me.magnum.melonds.impl.FileSystemRomsRepository.access$loadCachedRoms(FileSystemRomsRepository.kt:38)
        at me.magnum.melonds.impl.FileSystemRomsRepository$getRoms$1$1.invokeSuspend(FileSystemRomsRepository.kt:86)
        at kotlin.coroutines.jvm.internal.BaseContinuationImpl.resumeWith(ContinuationImpl.kt:33)
        at kotlinx.coroutines.DispatchedTask.run(DispatchedTask.kt:108)
        at kotlinx.coroutines.internal.LimitedDispatcher$Worker.run(LimitedDispatcher.kt:115)
        at kotlinx.coroutines.scheduling.TaskImpl.run(Tasks.kt:103)
        at kotlinx.coroutines.scheduling.CoroutineScheduler.runSafely(CoroutineScheduler.kt:584)
        at kotlinx.coroutines.scheduling.CoroutineScheduler$Worker.executeTask(CoroutineScheduler.kt:793)
        at kotlinx.coroutines.scheduling.CoroutineScheduler$Worker.runWorker(CoroutineScheduler.kt:697)
        at kotlinx.coroutines.scheduling.CoroutineScheduler$Worker.run(CoroutineScheduler.kt:684)
        Suppressed: kotlinx.coroutines.internal.DiagnosticCoroutineContextException: [StandaloneCoroutine{Cancelling}@7c547ee, Dispatchers.IO]
```

In the above case, `SevenZRomFileProcessor` was trying to alloc ~536 MB.  It looks like the `org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.sevenz.SevenZFile` library is allocating a dictionary of between ~25 MB and ~500+ MB, based on some aspects of the 7z file (e.g. the dictionary used to (de)compress the 7z).

I've seen `OutOfMemoryError`s trigger with ~25 MB allocs, ~128 MB allocs, ~256 MB allocs and more, all at this location.

The `SevenZRomFileProcessor` ROM processor [was changed a while back](https://github.com/nicjansma/melonDS-android/commit/5c6dbcfd83ca7f2e077f8b49b0646c68f3a3f084) to try to protect itself from allocating too much when decoding 7z files:

```kt
val sevenZFile = SevenZFile.Builder()
    .setMaxMemoryLimitKb((deviceMemory * 0.1f).toKB().toInt())
    .setSeekableByteChannel(fileStream.channel)
    .get()
```

Here, it's trying to limit max memory to 10% of RAM.  As noted for e.g. Ayn Thor, this would be ~800 MB (Lite/Base), ~1.2 GB (Pro) or ~1.6 GB (Max) limitation -- which is higher than the allocations that are crashing the app.

From what I can gather, the issue is that **there are two coroutine scopes that are helping build the games list, which are multithreaded and are making large allocations in parallel**.  When this happens, there may be enough outstanding allocations that OOM beyond the heap allowed for the app:

* One scope reads the file name of ROMs from any matching files, and adds it to the games list
* Next (in parallel), another scope reads the icon from the ROM, and displays it for the game

These scopes are in `FileSystemRomsRepository` and `RomIconProvider`, and both use `Dispatchers.IO` threading.

From my understanding, the default `Dispatchers.IO` will create a thread pool equal to the number of CPU cores, which on the Thor (non-Lite) is 8.

As a result, when building the initial games list (+ icons), we will have two separate work queues that are running up to 8 tasks in parallel, each task allocating anywhere from 25 MB to 536 MB (per file).

This is why we're seeing so frequent crashes, though they are random in timing -- if multiple large allocations (on separate) threads are happening at once, we rapidly run out of RAM and OOM.

To address this, I've made a few targeted changes:

* The `FileSystemRomsRepository` and `RomIconProvider` are both limited to one thread (game names and icons still flow in very quickly)
* The `SevenZRomFileProcessor` catches `OutOfMemoryError` and tries to move on, without crashing the app
* The `AndroidManifest.xml` was updated to use `android:largeHeap="true"` which seems to decrease the liklihood of crashes as well

I've seen issues related to this referenced in:

* https://github.com/rafaelvcaetano/melonDS-android/issues/1519
* https://github.com/rafaelvcaetano/melonDS-android/issues/540 (maybe)

issues.title: Fix ROM not found error when launching from external apps
issues.body:
## Problem
Launching a ROM into melonDS from an external app (ES-DE in my case) via an explicit Intent with a content:// URI shows "Could not find ROM", even though the same file launches fine from melonDS's own ROM list.

## Root cause
Internal launches hand the emulator an already-resolved Rom object directly, so they never touch URI-matching logic. External launches only provide a bare content:// URI, which goes through FileSystemRomsRepository.getRomAtUri(). That function's matching strategies (findRomByPath, findRomBySize) work by opening the incoming URI via openFileDescriptor to resolve/compare its real path — but the sending app usually holds its own independent SAF permission grant over the ROM, obtained through its own folder picker, separate from melonDS's own persisted grant over the same file. melonDS has no permission on that external grant, so every open attempt throws SecurityException, which is silently swallowed, and every match strategy fails, falling through to a "ROM not found" error.

## Fix
DocumentsContract.getDocumentId() / getTreeDocumentId() are pure string-parsing calls on the URI itself — no IPC, no permission required. This adds a new matching strategy, findRomByDocumentId(), that parses the document ID out of both the incoming URI and each already-scanned ROM's own URI and compares them directly, before ever trying to open the file. If they match, the already-known Rom is returned immediately, bypassing the unpermitted incoming URI entirely.
